title: Public object storage exposure
blurb: Customer data bucket left public. Good for IR + threat-model retrofit interviews.

project.name: Customer document storage
project.description: SaaS feature that stores customer-uploaded documents in cloud object storage.

threats.name: Public bucket listing and download
threats.description: Bucket ACL/policy allows anonymous read; scanners enumerate and exfiltrate documents.

threats.name: Guessable object keys
threats.description: Sequential or predictable keys enable enumeration even with listing disabled.

threats.name: Long-lived signed URL leakage
threats.description: Presigned URLs with long TTL leak via logs, Referer, or support tickets.

mitigations.name: Block public access
mitigations.description: Account-level block public access; private bucket; deny anonymous principals.

mitigations.name: Unpredictable object keys
mitigations.description: Random object keys; no directory listing; authorize downloads through the app.

mitigations.name: Short-lived presigned URLs
mitigations.description: Short TTL, minimal scope, strip Referer where possible, avoid logging full URLs.

prompts.title: You just found flow-public-read in production for two weeks. What is your first hour?
prompts.answerMarkdown: Contain: remove public access / enable block public access. Preserve evidence: access logs, policy versions, config history. Scope: which prefixes, which tenants, whether objects were listed or downloaded. Notify security IC / legal if customer data may be exposed. Do not start with a long redesign; contain first, then investigate.

prompts.title: What was missing from the original threat model that allowed this?
prompts.answerMarkdown: Likely missing: anonymous internet actor, public-read dataflow, asset sensitivity on the bucket, and a control requiring private ACLs plus CI checks. Good answer names the absent element in OTM terms (actor, flow, threat, mitigation) and the verification that would have caught it (policy-as-code, CSPM).

prompts.title: After containment, how do you verify customers are safe and the class of bug will not return?
prompts.answerMarkdown: Review access logs for unauthorized GETs; rotate any exposed documents if needed; customer notification per legal. Prevention: org-level block public access, IaC policy deny, continuous scanning, and a design rule that downloads go through authenticated app URLs only. Track as a recurring control, not a one-off ticket.
